physicalNotes: Radius 0.08921418 Jupiter radii from Zúñiga-Fernández et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A..85Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A..85Z/abstract): 6,378.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00306 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Zúñiga-Fernández et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A..85Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZUNIGA_FERNANDEZ_ET_AL_2025): P 2.28909 d
sources.shape: Zúñiga-Fernández et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A..85Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZUNIGA_FERNANDEZ_ET_AL_2025): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0205 au and stellar radius 0.2075 solar radii; Zúñiga-Fernández et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A..85Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZUNIGA_FERNANDEZ_ET_AL_2025): inclination 90.35 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Zúñiga-Fernández et al. 2025 (2025A&A...702A..85Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZUNIGA_FERNANDEZ_ET_AL_2025): transit mid-time 2459525.40333 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
